svg.text: Compact carrier board for the 30-pin ESP32 DevKit V1 (Bruno)
Top view (component side) of a perfboard cut to 14 x 17 holes, about 36 x 43 mm. Antenna end up, USB at the bottom.
The small parts sit UNDER the ESP32, between its two socket strips. Wires are soldered on the underside.
ESP32 (dashed): antenna end
← USB end of the ESP32

← GPIO 25 is the pin in column 3, row 9
← GPIO 26 is the pin in column 3, row 10
← GPIO 27 is the pin in column 3, row 11
← GND is the pin in column 3, row 15
← VIN is the pin in column 3, row 16
Shaded: one spare row at each end and spare column 14. Nothing is soldered
there; the printed box holds the board by them.
Narrow clone (pin rows 22.9 mm apart)? Its second row lands in column 12:
move D1, R3 and the orange run one column to the left.
How to read it
solid line: bare wire or solder bridge along the holes, underside
dashed curve: insulated wire, underside, joined only at its ends
black dot: a component leg or wire end goes in this hole
Cutting the board
• Keep 14 columns and 17 rows of holes.
• Score along the next row of holes on both faces and snap it over a table edge.
• File the edges smooth. The board should be about 35.6 x 43.2 mm.
Parts on the board
Sockets
two 15-way strips: column 3 and column 13, rows 2 to 16
col 4 row 9 to col 7 row 9
R2 1 kΩ
col 4 row 10 to col 7 row 10
col 9 row 16 to col 12 row 16
Q1 NPN
legs in col 9: C row 9, B row 10, E row 11
2N2222 / PN2222 / 2N3904 / S8050: flat face towards column 13
BC337 / BC547: flat face towards column 3
col 9 row 8 to col 12 row 8, stripe at col 12
C1 220 µF
+ leg col 4 row 16, – leg (stripe) col 4 row 15, bent over to lie flat
towards column 9. No wider than 6.3 mm
MOTOR
red col 1 row 6, black col 1 row 7
PAW
col 1 row 11 and col 1 row 12 (either way round)
LED
short leg col 1 row 15, long leg col 1 row 16
Three insulated wires underneath
LED +: col 7 row 9 to col 1 row 16
motor +: col 12 row 8 to col 1 row 6
motor -: col 9 row 8 to col 1 row 7
Build tips
• Everything under the ESP32 must stay below 10 mm. Push Q1 down to the board.
• Solder the low parts and all the wiring first, then the two socket strips,
with the ESP32 plugged into them so it sets their spacing. Connectors last.
• Black and red run side by side on rows 15 and 16: check there is no bridge.
• Check with a meter before plugging the ESP32 in: no beep between the
VIN pin hole and the GND pin hole in column 3.
